newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-SECURITY TIGHTENED FOR WIGAN MATCH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-SECURITY TIGHTENED FOR WIGAN MATCH.

text.p: Security will be stepped up at a Sydney rugby league ground next week for a match involving top English side Wigan.

Australian rugby league officials took the decision after hundreds of fans rioted on the Belmore Oval terraces following Monday's Super League match between Canterbury Bulldogs and Penrith Panthers. Three police officers were injured and four spectators arrested.
Wigan are due to play Canterbury in the opening round of the world club championship next Monday.
"Obviously, none of us wants to see that sort of violence at public places," Super League executive director Ian Frykberg was quoted as saying in Sydney's Daily Telegraph.
"It was very unfortunate and not something we want to see at any football match," he said.
Canterbury chief executive Bob Hagan said police and private security personnel will be increased for future matches at Belmore and video cameras would be installed to monitor crowds.
Hagan said the riot started when a police officer was thrown to the ground while trying to restrain one unruly fan.
Canterbury followers were upset late in the match, won 28-20 by Penrith, when a try was disallowed.
